items.title: Show HN: I built an open source video editor that you can control with an LLM
items.why_it_matters: A novice developer built and shipped an open-source video editor in just 3 days by heavily leveraging LLMs to handle complex UI and timeline logic. This is a perfect example of "vibe coding" a real, functional app from scratch without getting bogged down in tutorials. This week, clone the Donkey repository and look at how they structured their LLM command parser to see if you can use a similar pattern for filtering news in AI-ingest.

items.title: We replaced our Grafana stack with a single Claude Code skill
items.why_it_matters: The team at Frigade replaced their entire complex Grafana monitoring stack with a single custom skill written for Claude Code. This shows how powerful it is to extend your terminal agent rather than building heavy, separate dashboards. This week, write a simple custom bash script or Claude Code skill to automate your local Supabase database backup and Git commit workflow in one command.

items.title: Show HN: Proliferate- open-source, self-hostable Codex for any coding agent
items.why_it_matters: Proliferate is a new open-source, self-hostable AI IDE that lets you run Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor in a single unified workbench. Since you already use both Claude Code and Codex, this gives you a centralized playground to compare how they handle your codebase. This week, clone the Proliferate repo, run it locally, and try using it to refactor one of your AI-ingest API routes.

items.title: Claudette: Make Claude stop talking like a BuzzFeed article
items.why_it_matters: Claudette is a popular new open-source utility designed to strip out the annoying, verbose, and "BuzzFeed-style" conversational filler that Claude often outputs. Since you rely on Claude for vibe coding, making its output direct and concise will save you significant reading time and token costs. This week, copy the system prompt rules from the Claudette README and add them to your local Claude Code config file to get cleaner, faster code responses.

items.title: Turn Claude Code into a 24/7 Agent
items.why_it_matters: The claude-code-hermit project lets you run Claude Code continuously in the background as a persistent agent. Instead of waiting for Claude to finish writing code while you watch the terminal, you can queue up tasks and let it run. This week, install the hermit agent and set it to autonomously write unit tests for your Supabase integration while you focus on designing the frontend.

items.title: Quick impressions: A week of using Codex more than Claude
items.why_it_matters: A developer shared their practical takeaways after swapping their primary coding tool from Claude to Codex for a week, highlighting where Codex wins on context handling and speed. Since you use both tools, understanding their real-world trade-offs helps you direct them more effectively. This week, try switching your next feature build entirely to Codex for one session to see if its speed beats Claude Code for your Next.js setup.

items.title: Claude has a "Concise" output style
items.why_it_matters: Anthropic officially documented Claude's "Concise" output style, which instructs the model to omit explanations and deliver raw code. This is a built-in way to stop Claude from over-explaining things you already know. This week, append the concise flag or system prompt to your next Claude Code session to get straight-to-the-point code blocks without conversational filler.
